You need to tell FastAPI about the prefix by setting the **root path**. If your proxy strips the prefix before forwarding requests, you can configure the server with `fastapi run --root-path`[1]. For your `/api` prefix:

```console
fastapi run --root-path /api
```

**Why the docs break:** when you open the integrated docs UI (the frontend), it would expect to get the OpenAPI schema at `/openapi.json`[1] rather than under your prefix, so it can't load the schema. The docs UI would also need the OpenAPI schema to declare that this API `server` is located at[1] the prefix.

With the root path set, FastAPI uses this `root_path` to create the default `server` in OpenAPI with the URL provided by `root_path`.[3]

**What to expect:** The docs page should then work at the proxied URL, such as `/api/docs`. If you try the docs UI served by the server directly, without the path prefix in the URL, it won't work, because it expects to be accessed through the proxy.[3]

The FastAPI docs I found use Traefik as the example proxy, so they don't cover Nginx-specific configuration. For the full walkthrough, see https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/behind-a-proxy/
